t: The Shishmaref Airport, conveyed to the State of Alaska on January 5, 1967, in Patent No. 1240529, is subject to reversion to the United States, pursuant to the terms of that patent for nonuse as an airport. The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration is hereby directed to exercise said reverter in Patent No. 1240529 in favor of the United States within twelve months of the date of enactment of this section. Upon revesting of title, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the United States shall immediately thereafter transfer all right, title, and interest of the United States in the subject lands to the Shishmaref Native Corporation. Nothing in this section shall relieve the State, the United States, or any other potentially responsible party of liability, if any, under existing law for the cleanup of hazardous or solid wastes on the property, nor shall the United States or Shishmaref Native Corporation become liable for the cleanup of the property solely  by virtue of acquiring title from the State of Alaska or from the United States.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that because the State of Alaska and the Shishmaref Native Corporation (both outside the federal government) are named, outsiders are involved in a federal decision. But Congress simply directs the FAA Administrator to exercise the reverter and transfer title, with no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. The outside parties are only the source and recipient of the land, and the liability clause merely preserves existing law.
fable.s: The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration is hereby directed to exercise said reverter in Patent No. 1240529 in favor of the United States within twelve months of the date of enactment of this section.

opus.w: Congress orders the FAA Administrator to take back the airport land and then requires the United States to transfer it to the Shishmaref Native Corporation. It provides no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. The State and the Native Corporation are mentioned only as the party losing title and the party receiving it, not as participants in the decision. The liability clause preserves existing law and gives no one a new right to challenge the decision.
opus.s: The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration is hereby directed to exercise said reverter in Patent No. 1240529 in favor of the United States within twelve months of the date of enactment of this section.
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** The section names outside parties: the State of Alaska, the Shishmaref Native Corporation and "other potentially responsible" parties. That could make it look like participation. But Congress itself directs every step here. The FAA Administrator must exercise the reverter, and the United States must then transfer the land. Nobody outside the government is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to object or sue before any federal decision. The Native Corporation simply receives the land, and the liability clause only keeps existing law in place.

qwen_chat.w: The section mandates a specific sequence of actions (reversion and transfer) to be carried out by federal officials. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or input from the Shishmaref Native Corporation or any other outside party before these actions are taken. The transfer is a unilateral statutory directive, not a participatory decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration is hereby directed to exercise said reverter in Patent No. 1240529 in favor of the United States within twelve months of the date of enactment of this section. Upon revesting of title, notwithstanding any other provision of law, the United States shall immediately thereafter transfer all right, title, and interest of the United States in the subject lands to the Shishmaref Native Corporation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the transfer of land to the Shishmaref Native Corporation involves coordination with an outside entity (the tribe/corporation). However, the text describes a mandatory, unilateral action by the federal government ("is hereby directed to exercise said reverter... shall immediately thereafter transfer"). There is no requirement for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from the Shishmaref Native Corporation or any other outside party before the decision to transfer is made. The transfer is a direct statutory command, not a participatory process.
